comments.author: @universebecomingltd
comments.text:
Your reference to the alien narrative has certainly captivated my interest. Though it initially fell outside my primary focus, considering the mention of actual aliens during the hearing, I am now inclined to delve deeper into the matter.

Moving on to the speculation regarding Shopify potentially replacing its customer service workforce with AI, it strikes me as rather ironic. Given the accelerating pace of advancements in AI capabilities - specifically in areas such as auto-generating efficient code (as evidenced by innovations like GPT Engineer), I foresee a future where Shopify itself may be supplanted. It is indeed possible that in a few years, any software application desired by a user will be dynamically crafted by AI, thus rendering traditional software-based businesses like Shopify obsolete.

Lastly, Wes, I must commend your impeccable performance. You project an exceptionally likable and intelligent persona on camera. Maintain this trajectory, and your future looks promising!

comments.author: @reinerheiner1148
comments.text: Replacing customer service is only the first step in replacing higher skilled professions. I see a tsunami of unemployment coming, and it will probably start in lower income countries where many western companies get their remote work customer service personel from. From there, it will crawl to the higher skilled population. This is going to be a wild ride... and the economy will have no choice but to adapt fundamentally. The higher the skill demand, the longer it will take ai to take over, but the timeline for this is anyones guess. Probably sooner then we might think. In the short and medium term, AI might be limited by the supply of AI accelerators that the industry is able to provide. The safest professions will be those guarded by governments, and manual labor, for now. But honestly, I see a future that is either absolute horror ( with a wide variety of horror scenarios) or absolute bliss, where AI and robots basically do everything leaving humans to do whatever they want. Absolutely wild...

You've all got this backwards, including the people investing on AI customer service. It'll scour the frequently asked questions, and communicate with other virtual agents for further information clarification, and it will be your front end for interacting with the world.  
There will not be a need for customer service agents at all because we'll all have perfect service in our pocket, catered to ourselves.
